```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("Stochastic_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 5  # sources
    J = 5  # destinations
    S = 10  # scenarios
    alpha = 0.9  # confidence level
    max_violations = int(math.floor((1 - alpha) * S))

    supplies = [179, 89, 127, 143, 157]
    recourse_caps = [71, 35, 50, 57, 62]
    base_costs = [[19.9, 5.8, 22.31, 8.03, 19.52], [23.63, 6.98, 13.31, 7.14, 23.73], [16.02, 8.94, 21.37, 13.3, 18.12], [12.18, 5.3, 20.69, 24.03, 19.63], [22.35, 5.13, 5.43, 13.27, 24.65]]
    recourse_costs = [[39.8, 11.6, 44.62, 16.06, 39.04], [47.26, 13.96, 26.62, 14.28, 47.46], [32.04, 17.88, 42.74, 26.6, 36.24], [24.36, 10.6, 41.38, 48.06, 39.26], [44.7, 10.26, 10.86, 26.54, 49.3]]
    demand_scenarios = [[25, 12, 11, 16, 25], [29, 13, 12, 25, 32], [27, 12, 10, 18, 35], [25, 11, 12, 15, 37], [23, 10, 13, 24, 21], [23, 13, 9, 20, 22], [19, 12, 9, 24, 25], [22, 13, 10, 18, 23], [23, 12, 12, 22, 27], [22, 12, 12, 23, 37]]

    # Big-M: largest demand * 2
    M = max(demand_scenarios[s][j] for s in range(S) for j in range(J)) * 2

    # --- Variables ---
    # Stage 1: base shipments
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Base_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Stage 2: recourse shipments per scenario
    y = {}
    for s in range(S):
        for i in range(I):
            for j in range(J):
                y[(i,j,s)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Recourse_S{i}_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # Violation indicators
    z = {}
    for j in range(J):
        for s in range(S):
            z[(j,s)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Violate_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # --- Objective: minimize base cost + expected recourse cost ---
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(base_costs[i][j] * x[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J))
        + (1.0 / S) * quicksum(recourse_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j,s)]
                               for s in range(S) for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply (base)
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"SupplyBase_S{i}")

    # C2: Supply (recourse per scenario)
    for i in range(I):
        for s in range(S):
            m.addConstr(
                quicksum(y[(i,j,s)] for j in range(J)) <= recourse_caps[i],
                name=f"SupplyRecourse_S{i}_Sc{s}")

    # C3: Demand chance constraint (SAA)
    for j in range(J):
        for s in range(S):
            m.addConstr(
                quicksum(x[(i,j)] + y[(i,j,s)] for i in range(I))
                + M * z[(j,s)] >= demand_scenarios[s][j],
                name=f"DemandChance_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # C4: Violation budget per destination
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(z[(j,s)] for s in range(S)) <= max_violations,
            name=f"ViolationBudget_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

To: Operations Leadership Team
From: Supply Chain Director
Subject: Two-Stage Shipping Plan under Demand Uncertainty
Date: Today

Challenge
We need to set a dependable shipping plan from our warehouses to stores despite uncertain customer demand. Locking in shipments too low risks stockouts and lost sales; locking in too high ties up working capital and increases handling. A structured approach is required to protect the customer experience and manage costs without relying on perfect forecasts.

Two-Phase Approach
- Phase 1 (Base plan): Commit to an advance shipping schedule from each warehouse to each store before actual demand is known. This plan must respect available inventory at each warehouse and leverage our regular lanes at standard rates.
- Phase 2 (Emergency response): After demand is revealed in each forecast scenario, use expedited or emergency shipments to cover any shortfalls. Emergency shipments draw from separate, more limited capacities and carry higher per-unit costs. The base plan remains fixed; only the emergency response adjusts to the realized demand.

Reliability Target
We will design the plan so each store is fully supplied in most forecasted demand scenarios, reflecting our agreed service level. A small fraction of scenarios may fall short, acknowledging rare spikes or outliers. This balances customer service with practical cost control.

Cost Focus
The plan will aim to lower our total expected cost by:
- Keeping base shipments cost-effective across lanes while staying within warehouse inventory.
- Limiting the use of more expensive emergency shipments, but deploying them when needed to meet demand and uphold service levels.
- Evaluating performance across the full set of demand scenarios and focusing on the average emergency cost rather than only the worst case.

Operational Guardrails
- Do not exceed available base inventory at any warehouse when setting the initial plan.
- Keep emergency shipments within their separate capacities and lane availability.
- Ensure each store meets the agreed service level across the scenario set.
- Maintain a clear, auditable linkage from forecasts to shipment decisions so we can update the plan as assumptions change.

Next Steps
- Confirm the service level target, scenario set, lane costs, and available inventories.
- Generate a base shipment plan that respects inventory and keeps regular-lane usage efficient.
- Stress-test the plan across all demand scenarios, quantify emergency needs, and iterate to improve the cost–reliability trade-off.
- Finalize the plan, communicate warehouse and carrier allocations, and put monitoring in place to trigger emergency actions when actual demand diverges from plan.
